newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Kelon sees big China demand for fridges.
newsitem.headline: Kelon sees big China demand for fridges.

text.p: Guangdong Kelon Electrical Holdings Co Ltd said on Friday it sees bright prospects due to the fast-growing refrigerator market in China.

"We estimate that there is an underlying demand of 80 million units of refrigerators in China between 1996 and 2000," Wang Guoduan, vice president of corporate administration and planning, said in a company presentation.
Wang said strong demand was being fuelled by growing wealth among Chinese people, Beijing's reforms allowing people to buy their own homes and the need to replace old units.
"We have manufacturing orders on hand of 2.1 million units for 1997 compared with our production capacity of 1.8 million units," said vice president Don Lee.

The company said its production capacity would gradually be increased to 2.3 million units in 1998, 2.8 million units in 1999 and 3.5 million units in 2000 when all four of its manufacturing plants in China are in operation.
Kelon said its market share increased to 17.1 percent as at the end of 1996 from 13.5 percent in 1995.
Wang said Kelon would further develop its sales force and open 26 regional offices throughout China this year. It also plans to develop a nationwide production network, he said.
"We plan to acquire component manufacturers (in China), likely in the second half of 1997, as part of our vertical integration plan," Lee said.
Lee said the company's gross profit margin was 30.8 percent in 1996 and was likely to increase on expectation of lower costs of raw materials and improvements in production efficiency.
On Friday, Kelon reported a 55.2 percent rise in net profit to 439.8 million yuan for year ended December 31, 1996.
